regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not present non-registered persons as modern-medicine practitioners
description: No person other than a doctor with an MCI-recognised qualification registered with the Medical Council of India/State Medical Council may practise the modern system of medicine or surgery. A person qualified in any other system of medicine is not allowed to practise modern medicine in any form.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Promote only scientifically founded methods of healing
description: A physician should practise methods of healing founded on a scientific basis and should not associate professionally with anyone who violates this principle.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Display the medical council registration number
description: Every physician shall display the registration number accorded by the State Medical Council/Medical Council of India in the clinic and on all prescriptions, certificates and money receipts given to patients. Failure to display it is professional misconduct under 7.3.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Use only recognised degrees and honours as name suffixes
description: Physicians shall display as suffix to their names only recognised medical degrees or such certificates/diplomas and memberships/honours which confer professional knowledge or recognise an exemplary qualification/achievement. Violation is professional misconduct under 7.3.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Prescribe by generic name and state drug composition
description: Every physician should prescribe drugs with generic names legibly and preferably in capital letters and ensure rational prescription and use of drugs. Drugs prescribed or supplied should explicitly state the proprietary formula as well as the generic name (6.3), and all drugs prescribed should carry a proprietary formula and clear name (6.5).

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Announce fees upfront; never offer 'no cure no payment'
description: A physician should announce fees before rendering service, and remuneration should be in the form and amount specifically announced to the patient. It is unethical to enter into a contract of "no cure no payment".

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Comply with Drugs and Magic Remedies Act and allied laws
description: A physician shall observe the laws regulating medical practice and not assist others to evade them, including the Drugs and Cosmetics Act 1940, NDPS Act 1985, MTP Act 1971, Transplantation of Human Organs Act 1994, Pre-natal Sex Determination Test Act 1994 and the Drugs and Magic Remedies (Objectionable Advertisement) Act 1954.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not exaggerate or minimise gravity of conditions
description: The physician should neither exaggerate nor minimise the gravity of a patient's condition.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Display fees clearly with full name, designation and registration
description: A physician shall clearly display fees and other charges on the board of the chamber and/or hospitals visited, and prescriptions should make clear if the physician dispensed any medicine. The prescription letterhead shall carry the physician's full name and designation along with registration particulars.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not solicit patients directly or indirectly
description: Soliciting of patients directly or indirectly, by a physician, a group of physicians, or by institutions or organisations is unethical.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not advertise a doctor's skill, qualifications or achievements
description: A physician shall not make use of himself/herself or his/her name as the subject of any form of advertising or publicity, through any mode, alone or with others, that invites attention to his professional position, skill, qualification, achievements, attainments, specialities, appointments, associations, affiliations or honours, or that would ordinarily result in self-aggrandisement.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not let doctors endorse drugs, devices or commercial products
description: A physician shall not give any person, for compensation or otherwise, any approval, recommendation, endorsement, certificate, report or statement about any drug, medicine, nostrum remedy, surgical or therapeutic article, apparatus, appliance or commercial product (or any test, demonstration or trial thereof) for use with his name, signature or photograph in any form of advertising through any mode.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not boast of cases, operations, cures or remedies
description: A physician shall not boast of cases, operations, cures or remedies or permit the publication of reports thereof through any mode.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Limit press announcements to the seven permitted purposes
description: A medical practitioner may make a formal announcement in the press only regarding: (1) starting practice, (2) change of type of practice, (3) changing address, (4) temporary absence from duty, (5) resumption of another practice, (6) succeeding to another practice, and (7) public declaration of charges.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not print doctor's photograph on letterheads or signboards
description: Printing a self-photograph or any such publicity material on the letterhead or on the signboard of the consulting room or any clinical establishment is self-advertisement and unethical conduct. Printing sketches, diagrams or pictures of the human system is not unethical.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not run an open shop selling medicines or appliances
description: A physician should not run an open shop for sale of medicine for dispensing prescriptions of other doctors or for sale of medical or surgical appliances. Prescribing or supplying drugs, remedies or appliances is not unethical so long as there is no exploitation of the patient.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not offer commissions, rebates or fee-splitting for referrals
description: A physician shall not give, solicit, receive or offer any gift, gratuity, commission or bonus for referring, recommending or procuring any patient, nor participate in division, rebating, splitting or refunding of any fee for treatment. This applies equally to referral of specimens or material for diagnostic purposes.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not prescribe or promote secret remedies
description: Prescribing or dispensing secret remedial agents of unknown composition, or the manufacture or promotion of their use, is unethical and prohibited. All drugs prescribed should carry a proprietary formula and clear name.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not offer or promote euthanasia
description: Practising euthanasia constitutes unethical conduct. Withdrawal of life support after brain death shall be decided only by a team of doctors (doctor in charge, CMO/MO in charge of the hospital and a nominated hospital doctor) or per the Transplantation of Human Organs Act 1994.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not accept pharma gifts, travel, hospitality or cash
description: A medical practitioner shall not receive any gift, travel facility (rail, road, air, ship, cruise tickets, paid vacations, incl. as conference/CME delegate) for self/family, individual hospitality such as hotel accommodation, or cash/monetary grants for individual purpose from the pharmaceutical or allied healthcare industry; research funding may be received only through approved institutions, transparently and fully disclosed. Penalties per item value: above Rs 1,000 up to Rs 5,000 censure; Rs 5,000-10,000 removal from register for 3 months; Rs 10,000-50,000 removal for 6 months; Rs 50,000-1,00,000 removal for 1 year; above Rs 1,00,000 removal for more than 1 year.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Disclose source and amount of industry research funding
description: A practitioner undertaking industry-funded research must ensure regulatory permission, ethics committee clearance and legal compliance, that the source and amount of funding is publicly disclosed at the beginning itself, and that he retains freedom to publish results. Violation: first-time censure, thereafter removal from the register for a period depending on the violation.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Disclose doctors' pharmaceutical industry affiliations transparently
description: A practitioner may work for the pharmaceutical/allied healthcare industry as adviser, consultant, researcher or treating doctor, but must maintain professional autonomy and integrity, not compromise patients' interests, keep affiliations lawful and ensure they are fully transparent and disclosed. Violation: first-time censure, thereafter removal from the register.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not let doctors publicly endorse industry drugs or products
description: A medical practitioner shall not endorse any drug or product of the industry publicly; any study on the efficacy of such products shall be presented to/through appropriate scientific bodies or published in appropriate scientific journals. Violation: first-time censure, thereafter removal from the register.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not advertise or offer sex determination tests
description: On no account shall a sex determination test be undertaken with intent to terminate the life of a female foetus, unless there are other absolute indications under the MTP Act 1971. Termination of a normal female foetus amounting to female foeticide is professional misconduct leading to penal erasure and criminal liability.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not issue untrue, misleading or improper certificates
description: A practitioner who signs or gives under his name any certificate, notification, report or similar document that is untrue, misleading or improper is liable to have his name deleted from the Register. A practitioner shall not issue certificates of efficiency in modern medicine to unqualified or non-medical persons (7.10).

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not offer steroids, psychotropics or Schedule H/L drugs improperly
description: Prescribing steroids/psychotropic drugs without absolute medical indication, or selling Schedule 'H' and 'L' drugs and poisons to the public except to one's own patient, in contravention of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, is gross professional misconduct.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not use lay-press articles or interviews for self-promotion
description: A physician should not contribute articles or give interviews to the lay press regarding diseases and treatments which may have the effect of advertising himself or soliciting practice. Writing under his own name on public health or hygienic living, public lectures and radio/TV/internet talks for that purpose are permitted.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Restrict institution ads to name, patients, facilities and fees
description: An institution run by a physician (maternity home, nursing home, private hospital, rehabilitation centre, training institution etc.) may be advertised in the lay press, but the advertisement should contain nothing more than the name of the institution, type of patients admitted, type of training and other facilities offered, and the fees.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Keep signboards modest and limited to permitted particulars
description: It is improper to use an unusually large signboard or write on it anything other than the physician's name, qualifications from a University or statutory body, titles, speciality, and registration number with the name of the State Medical Council; prescription papers should carry the same contents. Affixing a signboard on a chemist's shop or where the physician does not reside or work is improper.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not disclose patient secrets in public content
description: A practitioner shall not disclose patient secrets learnt in professional practice except in a court of law under the Presiding Judge's orders, where there is a serious and identified risk to a specific person and/or community, or for notifiable diseases.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not publish identifiable patient photos or cases without consent
description: A registered medical practitioner shall not publish photographs or case reports of patients in any medical or other journal in a manner by which their identity could be made out, without their permission. Consent is not needed if identity is not disclosed.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not use touts or agents to procure patients
description: A physician shall not use touts or agents for procuring patients.

regulation: IMC (Professional Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations 2002
title: Do not claim specialist status without special qualification
description: A physician shall not claim to be a specialist unless he has a special qualification in that branch.
